title: Hyper-Relational Knowledge Graph Representation Learning Based on Multi-Granularity Semantic Aware Message Passing

problem.claim: HKG representation learning must integrate entity-level roles and hyperedge-level properties to mitigate information loss.

gap.claim: Conventional message passing operates only along hyperedges and often inadequately learns multi-granularity semantics.

contributions.claim: HyperSMP propagates information between entities and hyperedges to aggregate entity-level roles at the hyperedge level while preserving semantic and structural information.
A fine-grained aggregation layer uses entity-level attention to aggregate different entity roles in hyperedge embeddings.
A granularity-aligned propagation layer recursively propagates information from hyperedges to entities and properties to capture message-passing paths in and out of hyperedges.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On public datasets, the authors report that HyperSMP outperforms state-of-the-art methods by at least 9.66% in F1 score.

narrative_sequence.summary: HKGs represent hyper-relational facts with rich semantics, where entities sharing a property can play different roles in a hyperedge.
Information loss arises because conventional message passing learns only one granularity and inadequately captures multi-grained semantics.
HyperSMP aggregates entity roles at the hyperedge level and aligns propagation between hyperedges, entities, and properties.
The unified hyperedge-level representation captures multi-grained semantics and high-order structure, while stacked layers discover multi-hop entity associations.
Experiments on public datasets report an F1-score advantage over state-of-the-art methods.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation protocol, or statistical significance of the reported F1 improvement.
